newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam floods kill 34, leave thousands homeless.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam floods kill 34, leave thousands homeless.

text.p: At least 34 people died and tens of thousands were left homeless by heavy flooding in Vietnam's central provinces at the end of last week, officials and state-controlled media said on Tuesday.

There had previously been only sketchy and conflicting media reports of deaths and damage caused by the low tropical atmospheric depression, which brought torrential rains and high winds and cut telecommunication links.
An official at the Vietnam Red Cross said Ha Tinh province was the worst hit.
He said 17 people had died in flooding there and 166,180 had been affected, of whom about 70 percent were in need of emergency relief.
Officials at the Central Committee for Flood and Storm Control were not available for comment on the disaster.
But the daily Vietnam News quoted the committee as saying that five people had died in both Quang Tri and Thua Thien-Hue, four in Quang Nam-Da Nang and three in Binh Dinh.

It said efforts to fly relief supplies by helicopter to Ha Tinh's hilly Huong Khe district had failed because of poor visibility. The district, where six people were reported to have died after 15 houses collapsed, was eventually reached by a convoy over land.
The Red Cross official said 9,160 hectares (22,634 acres) of the province's rice fields had been destroyed and material damage was estimated at $12.81 million.
The lastest disaster took to around 420 the number of people who have died in tropical storms and flooding in northern and central Vietnam since the beginning of July.
Vietnam suffers a string of floods and storms every year, most between July and October. Officials say damage to northern areas of the country this year has been the worst in a decade.
Storms and flooding usually arrive in the Mekong Delta, the country's southern rice bowl, at about the end of September.
